steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: British film narrative has distinctive traditions that differ from Hollywood's classical model, often prioritising social observation, character study and realism over goal-driven plot mechanics.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Social realism is a defining tradition in British cinema, presenting working-class life with authenticity, political awareness and a commitment to representing experiences that mainstream cinema typically ignores.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The kitchen sink tradition of the late 1950s and 1960s brought working-class domestic life to British screens with unprecedented frankness, challenging the middle-class conventions of earlier British cinema.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: British narratives often resist the classical Hollywood drive towards resolution, instead favouring open endings, unresolved conflicts and a sense that social problems cannot be solved by individual heroism.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Identify which British narrative tradition your set film belongs to and explain how it uses or challenges that tradition's conventions. Compare British narrative approaches with Hollywood to show what is distinctive about UK storytelling. Use specific scenes to illustrate how narrative choices — open endings, collective protagonists, regional settings — create meaning. Consider how narrative structure reflects cultural values: British cinema's resistance to closure reflects different assumptions about society than Hollywood's drive to resolution. Acknowledge that contemporary British films often blend traditions rather than fitting neatly into one category.
